title: Why we get a fever
examples: Why is a fever actually good for me?
How does my body know when it needs to raise the temperature?
What causes the body's thermostat to change?

explain.say: When germs enter your body, your immune system starts fighting them.
To fight these germs, your body needs to create a better fighting environment.
A higher temperature makes it harder for many types of germs to survive.
The brain contains a special part that acts like a thermostat for your body.
When the thermostat detects germs, it signals the body to raise the set point.
In real life, if you get a bad infection, your body can raise your temperature to help fight it.

faq.q: Is a fever always a sign that I am sick?
faq.a: A fever usually means your body is fighting something off. It is a sign of an immune response, not the illness itself.
asks: Does fever mean I have germs?
Is a high temperature always bad?

faq.q: Does the fever come from the germs themselves?
faq.a: No, the germs do not cause the fever. Your body's reaction to the germs causes the temperature to rise.
asks: Are the germs making me hot?
Where does the heat come from?

faq.q: If I take medicine to lower my fever, am I stopping the fight?
faq.a: Lowering the fever too much can sometimes slow down the immune response. Medicine helps you feel better, but the fever is part of the process.
asks: Should I always treat my fever?
Is it dangerous to have a fever?

faq.q: What exactly is the thermostat in my body?
faq.a: It is a part of your brain called the hypothalamus. It keeps your body temperature within a safe, normal range.
asks: Which part of the brain controls heat?
How does the body keep temperature stable?

faq.q: Can I get a fever from something that is not an infection?
faq.a: Sometimes, strong physical stress or certain medicines can cause a temperature change. However, the most common cause is fighting off germs.

facts: The immune system detects foreign invaders like bacteria and viruses.
The hypothalamus in the brain regulates the body's temperature.
A fever raises the body temperature to make it harder for germs to live.
The fever is a sign that the body is actively fighting an infection.

quiz.say: If germs enter your body, what system starts fighting them?
quiz.why: The immune system is responsible for defending the body against invaders like germs.

wrong.0: The brain controls the temperature, but it is not the fighting system.
wrong.1: The thermostat is the control unit, not the fighting mechanism itself.
wrong.2: Blood carries the components, but the immune system is the active defense.

quiz.say: What part of the brain acts like a thermostat?
quiz.why: The hypothalamus is the specific area in the brain that monitors and controls body heat.

wrong.1: The cortex is mainly for thinking and movement, not temperature control.
wrong.2: The spinal cord sends signals, but it does not regulate the set point for temperature.
wrong.3: A lobe is a general section of the brain, not the specific control center.

quiz.say: If the body temperature rises due to germs, what is this process called?
quiz.why: Fever is the measurable increase in body temperature caused by the immune response.

wrong.0: Infection is the cause (the germs), not the body's temperature response.
wrong.1: Immunity is the ability to fight, but fever is the physical manifestation of that fight.
wrong.3: Inflammation is a reaction at the site, but fever is the systemic temperature change.
